walkthroughs.body_html:
Anthropological Practice (Methods & Ethics) — a core area of Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Anthropological Practice (Methods & Ethics) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Anthropological Practice (Methods & Ethics).

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How does radical feminism differ from liberal feminism?
options: They are essentially the same with minor differences.
Radical feminists oppose all women's rights.
Schools have no influence on outcomes.
Radical feminists see patriarchy as the primary system of oppression requiring fundamental change.

mcqs.q: How did Marx define social class?
options: Radical feminists oppose all women's rights.
By relationship to the means of production: the bourgeoisie own productive resources; the proletariat sell their labour. Class is a structural relationship, not just income level.
Marx defined class by how much money people earn.
Marx defined class by occupational status like the Registrar General.
